reader.summary: 01-what-ai-agents-can-do.html 8/10, 02-the-genai-map.html 7/10. A newcomer would struggle most with the cost comparison in the second lesson: the build side never says whether its numbers are monthly, and seat is never explained.

history.summary: 01-what-ai-agents-can-do.html 8/10, 02-the-genai-map.html 7/10. A newcomer would struggle most with the cost comparison in the second lesson: the build side never says whether its numbers are monthly, and seat is never explained.

01-what-ai-agents-can-do.html 8/10, 02-the-genai-map.html 7/10. A newcomer would struggle most with the layer map, where the second lesson blurs the workflow and agent ideas from the first and the hawker analogy does not show what layer 3 does.

02-the-genai-map.html 7/10. A newcomer would get the four layers and the buy-or-build sums, but would struggle with the hawker-centre comparison, which never maps its parts to the layers, and with terms such as retrieval, agents and workflow builders that appear in the first picture before they are explained.

03-llms-pros-cons-risks.html 7/10. A newcomer would struggle most with the cost sum in Step 4, where the lesson never shows how a share of mistakes becomes a monthly loss, and with the dense risks-and-controls paragraph in Step 2.

03-llms-pros-cons-risks.html 7/10. A newcomer would be most stuck on the step that prices the checking: the formula multiplies minutes by an hourly rate without saying to convert minutes into hours, so the sum only makes sense from the worked box.

03-llms-pros-cons-risks.html 7/10. A newcomer would struggle most with the cost sum in Step 4, where the lesson jumps from minutes of checking straight to a dollar figure without showing the hourly-rate step.

03-llms-pros-cons-risks.html 7/10. A newcomer would grasp that checking should match the cost of a mistake, but would trip over the cost sum in Step 4 and a quiz explanation that contradicts its own answer.

04-who-sells-what-in-ai.html 7/10. A newcomer would get stuck at the break-even step, where seat cost means a per-person fee in one place and a whole-team total in another, and the cap and volume price in the quiz are never explained.

04-who-sells-what-in-ai.html 7/10. A newcomer would follow the six supplier types and the five vendor questions, but would get stuck on where the break-even number comes from, and on what one billable 'answer' and 'volume' mean.

01-what-scope-is.html 8/10, 02-gathering-requirements.html 8/10, 03-breaking-work-down.html 8/10, 04-spotting-scope-creep.html 8/10, 05-handling-a-change-request.html 8/10, 06-acceptance-and-sign-off.html 9/10. A newcomer would most likely trip on a few terms used before they are named, such as the in list, estimate and days of effort, and on money written differently in English and 中文 in the chan

09-rag-or-fine-tuning.html 8/10. A newcomer would most struggle with the side-by-side results: the table is English only and uses dollars while the quiz uses Singapore dollars, and it never says why the free prompt-only option loses.

10-scaling-laws-for-business.html 7/10, 11-new-ideas-and-traps.html 8/10. A newcomer would struggle most with the money sums: the pricing steps pack several numbers and terms (cost per answer, cost per month, the extra point, payback) into a few sentences, and 'fix' and the currency are used before they are pinned down.
